answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake of tokens in escrow, like ferrous ore sunk in a lagoon: cheap to drop in once, but every extra fake identity demands another full deposit, so an attacker flooding the network pays linearly for each puppet while honest agents pay once. Slashing burns the stake of any identity caught misbehaving, and reputation grows slowly like a juniper, so new identities start at zero trust and must earn it over time, making mass fakery expensive and slow.
